tagline: The smallest fox, with the biggest ears for its size
summary: The fennec is the smallest of all the dog family, a sand-coloured fox of the Sahara that spends the hot day in a burrow and hunts at night. Its enormous ears do two jobs at once: they shed body heat, and they pick up the sound of insects and rodents moving beneath the sand.
ability: giant ears for cooling and listening

stats.size: Body about 36–41 cm plus an 18–30 cm tail; about 0.8–1.5 kg
stats.habitat: Sandy desert and arid scrub; shelters in burrows by day
stats.range: Throughout the Sahara, east to Sinai and Arabia
stats.diet: Insects, small rodents, lizards, birds and eggs, plus roots, fruits and leaves

facts.title: All ears
facts.text: The fennec has the largest ears relative to its body size of any member of the dog family. They can reach 10–15 cm long on an animal that weighs little more than a kilogram.

facts.title: Radiators and radar
facts.text: Those ears dissipate heat, and they are sensitive enough for the fox to hear prey moving under the sand. Once it has located a meal, the fennec digs with all four feet to reach it.

facts.title: The smallest canid
facts.text: The fennec is the smallest of all canids. Adults weigh roughly 0.8–1.5 kg, smaller than many pet cats.

facts.title: No need to drink
facts.text: Fennecs can go for long periods, possibly indefinitely, without drinking free water. Much of their moisture comes from food, including fruit, leaves and roots.

facts.title: Fur-lined slippers
facts.text: The soles of the feet are thickly furred, protecting the pads from hot sand and giving grip on loose dunes.

facts.title: Night shift
facts.text: Fennecs spend the hottest hours in burrows they dig themselves and come out to hunt at night. A reflective layer behind the retina, the tapetum, helps them see in the dark.

notes: IUCN Least Concern per the Red List assessment by Wacher, Bauman & Cuzin, published 2015 (e.T41588A46173447); iucnredlist.org blocks automated fetching, so the category and year were confirmed via secondary citations of that assessment, not the live page. Size: Smithsonian gives 14–16 in body (about 36–41 cm), 7–12 in tail (18–30 cm); mass 0.8–1.5 kg from ADW (Smithsonian says 2–3 lb). Ear length 10–15 cm from Smithsonian (ADW says 15 cm). ADW's text still calls the species Data Deficient (an outdated listing) — not used. Images: the hero (Wiki Loves Earth Morocco 2017, featured picture) and alt-1 (WLE Algeria 2019) do not state whether the animals were wild or captive; four relaxed adults on a rock suggest they may be tame or kept, so setting is 'unknown'. alt-2 is a wild cub pair at a burrow (public domain, US publication 1980 without notice). Regions: sahara-arabia only — the range reaches Sinai, Kuwait and northern Nigeria/Chad edges, all within or bordering that region.
